From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French tourte.

Noun

[edit]

tourte (plural tourtes)

  1. (cooking) A kind of French pie.
    • 1812, B. Clermont, The Professed Cook, page 371:
      Make a Godiveaux farce as for the tourte under that name; cut the fillet of a neck of mutton into thin slices, and a few onions in the same manner; put some of the Godiveaux in the bottom of the pie, then some of the mutton, and slices of onions upon it, […]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • tourtre

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /tuʁt/
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

Ultimately from Latin turtur (“turtle, turtle dove, turtledove”). Compare tourterelle.

Noun

[edit]

tourte f (plural tourtes)

  1. (Quebec) passenger pigeon, Ectopistes migratorius
    Synonyms: tourte voyageuse, colombe voyageuse, pigeon migrateur
  2. (Louisiana) dove (clarification of this definition is needed (The English word "dove" does not have a strict definition - it refers to some species in Columbidae, with at least some traits similar to other so-called "doves" (those traits usually being small and/or white, but not necessarily); is this word a perfect match, or is it merely close/analogous?).)
Related terms
[edit]
  • tourtereau (masculine diminutive)
  • tourterelle (feminine diminutive)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Latin turta. Thought to derive from Latin tŏrta f (“twisted”), which would have yielded *torte in French.

Noun

[edit]

tourte f (plural tourtes)

  1. meat pie.
    Synonyms: pâté à la viande, (Quebec) tourtière
  2. Any kind of salted pie with vegetables, cheese etc, generally covered by undercrust (abaisse). Can be with fruits too.
Derived terms
[edit]
  • tarte
  • tourtière
  • tourte au fromage
Related terms
[edit]
  • tordre
